name: Customized Home
description: Customized Home lets every user reorganize the Jellyfin home screen: reorder sections by drag and drop, show or hide them, choose a display format per section (poster, landscape, square, size, titles) and search among all known sections. Optional hero banner at the top: a carousel of featured media (random, recently added, latest releases) with backdrop, logo, synopsis, ratings and play / resume / trailer / favorite actions. Adds its own sections without any other plugin: Continue Watching / Next Up combined, latest movies and shows by release date, collections, watch again, because you watched, genre. Works with the built-in sections and with sections added by other plugins (Home Screen Sections, ...). Administrators define a default layout. Web client only (browser, Jellyfin Desktop, the Android and iOS apps): native clients such as Android TV, Swiftfin or Kodi are not affected. Requires the File Transformation plugin.
overview: Easily edit and organize the sections on your homepage

versions.changelog: Readability of the administration page on a light dashboard: secondary text and the buttons of the destructive actions now meet the WCAG AA contrast minimum on both a light and a dark dashboard.
Readability of the administration page on a light dashboard: secondary text and the buttons of the destructive actions now meet the WCAG AA contrast minimum on both a light and a dark dashboard.

Housekeeping. The administration page asks its questions in the page instead of a browser prompt, like the editor does. The dots of the hero are easier to hit on a touch screen. At server start the layouts left behind by users deleted while the plugin was not running are removed. Saving the default layout or reading a genre thumbnail answers a readable error instead of a generic failure when the disk refuses, and a default layout that could not be written is no longer applied until the next restart.

Accessibility and robustness. Sections can be reordered without a pointer: arrow keys on the handle, or a Move up / Move down menu for touch and screen readers. The editor dialog keeps the keyboard focus, its menus follow the arrow keys, and closing it with unsaved changes asks first (in the page, no browser prompt). Hero: pause / play button, visible keyboard focus, header refreshed when switching tabs. Readable editor on a light dashboard, stylesheet fallbacks for older browsers and TVs, section keys built from titles in any script. Server: the layout of a deleted user is deleted with them, stored data survives unreadable or locked files, replaced genre thumbnails never serve stale bytes.

Reliability and privacy. Logging out or switching user in the same tab no longer keeps the previous user's layout and cached rows. Continue Watching / Next Up, Watch Again, Because You Watched and the hero are reloaded when the home page is shown again, without flicker. A failing server is retried with growing delays. A message explains why a layout is not applied or why the home page is empty, and how to fix it. Hero: favorite and watched now work on mobile and TV, "From the beginning" really restarts. The default layout no longer reveals libraries a user cannot access. "All genres" is displayed at once and loads its poster collages as the cards come into view. Layout uploads are size limited.
